methodological_rigor.justification: This preclinical study employs a rigorous multi-platform approach: SPR for quantitative KD measurement, flow cytometry-based multiplexed koff-rate screening (validated against SPR), Nur77-tdTomato reporter assays, xCelligence real-time impedance cytotoxicity, intracellular cytokine staining, chronic antigen stimulation, bioluminescence imaging xenograft models, and humanized NSG-SGM3 CRS models. The affinity library of 32 JCAR021 mutants covering a TCR-like to high-affinity spectrum is a systematic and comprehensive approach. Multiple biological replicates from independent healthy donors are used across experiments. scRNA-seq on bone marrow-isolated CAR-T cells provides mechanistic transcriptomic insight. Key limitations include small group sizes (n=4-8 mice per group), restriction to CD19-targeting 4-1BB co-stimulatory constructs, absence of CD28-based CAR comparison, and the use of healthy donor PBMCs rather than patient-derived cells. Statistical methods (ANOVA, log-rank, Mann-Whitney) are appropriate and consistently reported.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study (Oxford LoE 5) using cell lines, healthy donor T cells, and mouse xenograft/humanized CRS models. The affinity combination concept directly addresses major clinical limitations of approved CAR-T products (CRS toxicity, exhaustion, antigen escape) and proposes a concrete manufacturing strategy (50:50 JCAR017:JCAR021 mixture) testable in clinical trials. Proof-of-principle extension to anti-ROR1 CARs suggests target-agnostic applicability. The humanized NSG-SGM3 CRS model provides clinically translatable toxicity data. However, there is no clinical data, patient-derived tumor models, or co-stimulatory domain diversity, and the optimal affinity threshold and combination ratio remain undefined.

reporting_quality.justification: The study follows ARRIVE guidelines with IRB/ethics approval stated for both human samples and animal experiments. Experimental setup schematics, group sizes, donor numbers, and statistical tests are clearly reported. SPR, flow cytometry-based koff-rate, scRNA-seq pipeline (CellRanger 7.0.0, SCANPY v1.9.1), and analysis parameters are well-specified. Source data are stated as available. All figures include individual data points and statistical comparisons with defined reference groups. Limitations are explicitly acknowledged. The study is conducted under Nature Portfolio reporting summary standards. Primary sequencing data accession is not specified in the available text, and in vitro experiments lack explicit power calculations.

novelty_literature.justification: The affinity combination concept—mixing high- and low-affinity CARs targeting the same epitope in a single product—is a novel therapeutic strategy not previously systematically investigated. While individual properties of high- and low-affinity CARs are known, the demonstration that 50:50 combination reduces exhaustion in high-affinity CAR-T cells, limits CRS severity, and improves tumor clearance compared to either alone is a genuinely new finding. The systematic koff-rate library covering TCR-like to supra-physiological affinities and the identification of a minimum in vitro functionality threshold are methodologically novel. scRNA-seq evidence of reduced exhaustion gene expression in high-affinity CAR-T cells within combined products provides mechanistic depth not previously reported.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear logical structure: systematic affinity characterization → in vitro validation → in vivo efficacy → in vivo toxicity → in vitro combination → in vivo combination → scRNA-seq mechanistic analysis. Each section builds on the previous, and the rationale for affinity combination is well-motivated by observed limitations of each component alone. Results are reported with appropriate statistics and visualization. The limitations section is comprehensive, acknowledging restriction to 4-1BB/CD19 constructs, undefined optimal ratio, and immunocompromised model limitations. The discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within normal T-cell biology and prior CAR-T literature.

key_strengths: Novel affinity combination concept systematically validated across in vitro, in vivo efficacy, and humanized CRS toxicity models, addressing three simultaneous clinical limitations of current CAR-T products

Comprehensive scFv affinity library (32 JCAR021 mutants) with multiplexed flow cytometry-based koff-rate screening validated against SPR, covering an unprecedented affinity spectrum to TCR-like binding strengths

scRNA-seq evidence demonstrating that high-affinity JCAR017-T cells exhibit reduced exhaustion gene signatures when combined with low-affinity CARs provides mechanistic insight beyond phenotypic readouts
Humanized NSG-SGM3 CRS model recapitulating clinical dose-dependent toxicity provides clinically translatable safety data for the affinity combination strategy
Extension to anti-ROR1 CAR pair as proof-of-principle for target-agnostic applicability of the combination concept
key_concerns: All experiments use healthy donor-derived PBMCs; patient-derived T cells from heavily pretreated lymphoma/leukemia patients may behave differently, limiting direct translational inference
Mechanistic explanation for how low-affinity CAR-T cells reduce exhaustion in co-existing high-affinity CAR-T cells remains speculative (antigen competition hypothesis not formally tested)
Optimal combination ratio and lower affinity threshold for combination benefit are not defined; 50:50 ratio selected empirically without systematic optimization

All in vivo studies use CD19-targeting 4-1BB constructs; CD28 co-stimulatory domain (used in several approved products including axicabtagene ciloleucel) may have different exhaustion and CRS dynamics
Small group sizes (n=4-8 mice) in in vivo experiments and reliance on single tumor models (Raji/Nalm-6) limit statistical power for definitive conclusions about combination ratios
chief_reviewer.rationale: This high-quality preclinical study introduces and rigorously validates the affinity combination concept for CAR-T cell therapy, demonstrating simultaneous improvements in efficacy, safety, and persistence across multiple experimental systems; Tier 1 consideration is warranted given the paradigm-shifting nature of the finding, comprehensive multi-platform validation, and direct clinical translational relevance, with minor revisions to address mechanism and extend to CD28-based constructs.
